citation: [1638 S. Prairie Avenue — Shortall / Gregory house.] Halftone photograph of the street front of the Shortall (later Gregory) house, 1638 South Prairie Avenue, Chicago, from the Prairie Avenue walk; unknown photographer, undated. Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, 1638 S. Prairie.
author: unknown photographer (halftone)
repository: chicagology.com (secondary reproduction; the original holder is not named). Prairie library image a16-cgy-1638-gothic-photo, recorded there as 'link only'; the project's reference copy is in the image store (kevinrhaas/chicago-images, prairie-1904/files/a16-cgy-1638-gothic-photo.jpg).
locator: The whole print: the street front from the gable's south corner to the tower's north side, the front fence and its gate piers in the foreground.
rights_note: A secondary web reproduction whose original source and rights are not stated (the Prairie library's own ruling: 'unknown - link only'). Only forms, counts and proportions are read from it; nothing is derived from the image as an asset, and no copy is committed here.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-12 (T-2396) from the image store's reference copy, 900 x 1077 px greyscale, sha256 c57ee5e7463331d871a9ae4555fb95b8da8b8c2a3640a1a8a24fc907aa021646.
note: The only view of 1638's front this project reads. It is undated, and the Prairie library files it as later than 1904; the house stood through 1904 and nothing recorded changes its front, so its forms are carried to 1904 as inferred. It shows a frame front: a steep (about 52°) front gable with an oculus, a hooded pair of pointed windows over a one-storey canted bay of pointed lights, and at the north end a polygonal tower: an arched entrance porch on posts with pierced spandrels, double doors behind it and a stoop before it, and over the porch a regular octagonal upper stage with a pointed light in each street face, a cornice, and an octagonal spire to a finial whose point stands a little over the gable's apex. Proportions are read at the front's plane with the 1911 Sanborn sheet's 8.13 m front as the one length; no camera is solved from it yet (T-1865's image gate).
what_it_supplies: the corner tower: its octagonal plan, its width against the front, its stage's height over the porch, its pointed lights in the three street faces, its cornice and its spire to a finial
the porch under it as the tower's ground storey, entered through an arch
the front gable's pitch, oculus and hooded twin pointed windows, and the canted bay's pointed lights
what_it_does_not_supply: colour: the print is monochrome, so every paint colour stays reconstructed
the side, rear and north walls, and the roofs behind the gable
a date: undated, and its 1904 reading rests on nothing recorded as changing
